sections.overview: The common shelduck is a large, colourful waterfowl of coastal and inland wetlands across Eurasia.
sections.identification: It has a mainly white body, chestnut breast band, dark green head and red bill; the sexes are similar in plumage.
sections.habitat: It favours saline and brackish wetlands, including mudflats, estuaries and shallow coastal lakes; it also uses inland saline lakes.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on molluscs and other aquatic invertebrates, with plant material also included in its diet.
sections.behavior: Outside breeding, shelducks gather in flocks and many European birds assemble at moulting sites after breeding.
sections.reproduction: Pairs are monogamous and territorial; nests are often placed in cavities, and chicks soon leave the nest to feed with family groups.
sections.ecology: Its feeding on mudflat invertebrates links it closely to productive intertidal and estuarine wetlands.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment lists it as Least Concern and reports an increasing population trend (2019 assessment).
